question.text: If the normals of the parabola <math><msup><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></math> drawn at the end points of its latus rectum are tangents to the circle <math><msup><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, then the value of <math><msup><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></math> is equal to

solution.text:
End points of the latus rectum of the parabola y2=4x and 1,±2.
Equation of the normals at points 1,±2 are
y=-x+3 and y=x-3
rr x+y-3=0 and x-y-3=0
These lines are tangent to the circle x-32+y+22=r2
∴3±2-31+1=r=2 

Hence, r4=4
